item.title: Washington County de-claws FEMA clawback: County wins FEMA arbitration case
item.description: Washington County scored a major legal victory against the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), with an arbitration panel ruling in the county’s favor on February 27 after a long-standing funding dispute. FEMA notified the county in May 2024 that it would deny and de-obligate approximately $79.6 million for what the agency called ineligible hazard mitigation. item.title: Chipola Area Habitat for Humanity celebrates home sponsorship with Chipley Beef O’Brady’s
item.description: Chipola Area Habitat for Humanity (CAHFH) recently announced the completion and dedication of its 109th home, located at 730 Pecan Street in Chipley, Florida. CAHFH states the milestone was made possible through a significant partnership with Scott O’Brien and Salina O’Brien of Chipley Beef O’Brady’s, who served as the primary financial sponsor for the home. item.title: House approves tax cut for guns, camping gear, beer
item.description: The House passed a tax-cut bill Thursday aimed at saving money for campers, gun owners and drinkers of American-made beer. The House voted 105-2 on the plan (HB 7031), which drew criticism for lifting sales taxes next fiscal year on firearm accessories such as holsters, magazines, muzzle devices, sights and suppressors. item.title: Local youth shine at Washington County Youth Fair
item.description: The Washington County Youth Fair kicked off on Monday, February 23 at the Washington County Ag Center in Chipley, giving local youth a platform to showcase their skills, creativity, and showmanship. item.title: Stay on eviction order for Seacrest Wolf Preserve denied
item.description: Seacrest Wolf Preserve has been denied a request to delay its court‑ordered eviction, leaving the facility nine days to relocate several wolves and other wildlife currently housed at its Washington County property. item.title: Wausau Garden Club prepares pollinator gardens
item.description: The Wausau Garden Club is ready for spring, with members meeting on Thursday, March 5 to prepare plots for wildflower and pollinator gardens. The plots are located along the walking trail south of the Possum Palace in Wausau. Pictured above are members Al Hearn, Joe Tharp, DiAnne Hearn, and Lucinda Simonson.
